Admission seam (C4): the `Authenticator` Service Definition (`ctx.authenticator`) with its synchronous `admit(request, listener)` and `policy(listener)`, the `authenticator/policy` event, and the admission and policy types, which C4's `@delo/contract-admission` types are assignable to. It also declares `authenticator/minted` and `MintedCredential`, the announcement of each loopback credential Connection mints, by hash and never by value. No upstream composition provides it, so Connection keeps its built-in admission. Lead verdict: keep, after two independent review rounds (2026-11-07); the lead reviews this file line by line before it merges.

Admission seam (C4, loopback credential records): `BrowserAuth.create` takes an `onMint` callback, called synchronously with the credential's kind, the SHA-256 of its value, its audience, issue and expiry times and, for `/connect`, its Peer id, before the launch-token exchange or `/connect` writes the response that sets it. It never receives the credential's value. Without a callback nothing is called, so upstream's minting is unchanged. `writeUnauthorized` is public, so Connection answers a refused index or `/connect` request with the same 401. Lead verdict: keep, after two independent review rounds (2026-11-07); the lead reviews this file line by line before it merges.

Lead verdict: keep, after the independent review round of WP5.1 PR 2 (2026-11-07); the policy text, the nonce plumbing and the lazy evaluator were reviewed line by line, and the recorded real-model GIF run exercised the reach listener end to end.

Admission seam (C4): exports the `Authenticator` Service Definition, its types including `MintedCredential`, emits `authenticator/minted` from `BrowserAuth`'s mint callback, `LOOPBACK_LISTENER`, the reach listener types and `REACH_REFUSAL_STATUS`. The `/api` route adds a provider's `setCookie` to its response. For a Peer admitted on a reach listener, the index injections add the `__DSH_REMOTE_MEDIA__` global with the value `placeholder`; `reachContentSecurityPolicy` is exported. Lead verdict: keep, after the independent review round of WP5.1 PR 2 (2026-11-07); the policy text, the nonce plumbing and the lazy evaluator were reviewed line by line, and the recorded real-model GIF run exercised the reach listener end to end.

Admission seam (C4): reach listeners. `openReachListener` opens one only while an authenticator provider serves a valid reach policy for it, in a fiber that injects `authenticator`, so it closes before the provider is removed or replaced and never reopens by itself. Its dispatcher removes `tailscale-*` headers, refuses a foreign or loopback `Host`, a foreign SNI, a foreign or absent upgrade `Origin`, the launch token, `/connect` and `dsh-auth-*` cookies, then admits through the provider, sending a pre-login request only to its listed route. `builtinAdmission` exposes Connection's built-in loopback admission for providers to delegate to. The dispatcher also refuses a non-origin-form target and a second `Host` line, removes identity headers from the parsed, distinct and raw header views, records each admitted connection's session and device for `closeReachConnections`, and applies a policy change announced while the listener binds. Every reach response, refusals included, carries C4's security headers and a Content Security Policy with a fresh nonce, which the pass decision hands to the index renderer; the policy allows no string evaluation, images only from the origin, `data:` and `blob:`, and `no-store` covers `/auth/` and `/api`. The dispatcher records each admitted Peer so Connection can tell reach Peers apart. Lead verdict: keep, after two independent review rounds (2026-11-07); the lead reviews this file line by line before it merges.

Admission seam (C4): `admit` returns the dispatcher's Peer for a request a reach listener dispatched and refuses one it admitted as pre-login; a loopback request keeps the Host/Origin fence and then goes to the loaded authenticator provider, or to `builtinAdmission`, upstream's cookie admission unchanged, when none is loaded. `authorizeIndex` answers a reach request by its dispatcher's admission. `ctx.connection` gains `builtinAdmission` and `openReachListener`. A provider's `setCookie` reaches the RPC-channel response, `closeReachConnections` ends the reach connections of a session or device, and with a provider loaded the loopback index is admitted by it and the launch-token exchange at the root and `/connect` runs only while its loopback policy accepts the token. `isReachPeer` reports whether a Peer was admitted on a reach listener. Lead verdict: keep, after two independent review rounds (2026-11-07); the lead reviews this file line by line before it merges.

Admission seam (C4): `PeerAdmission`'s admitted result carries the provider's `setCookie`, and `ConnectionIndexResponse` may offer `setHeader`, through which an admitted loopback index response receives it. Lead verdict: keep, after two independent review rounds (2026-11-07); the lead reviews this file line by line before it merges.

Admission seam (C4, loopback credential records): proves that each launch-token exchange and each `/connect` mint announces `authenticator/minted` once, before the response is written, with the hash of the cookie value and never the value, and that requests minting nothing announce nothing. Lead verdict: keep, after two independent review rounds (2026-11-07); the lead reviews this file line by line before it merges.

Admission seam (C4): proves the reach dispatcher's refusals and their order over a real web server, that every route, upgrade, `/api` and the fallback answer 401 before sign-in, that pre-login requests reach only their listed route, that a listener opens only with a provider serving a valid reach policy and closes and stays closed when its provider is removed or replaced, and that loopback admission keeps the fence before a loaded provider. It also proves identity-header removal from every view on requests and upgrades, the refusal of non-origin-form targets and duplicate `Host` lines, that a policy withdrawn while binding opens no listener, that `closeReachConnections` ends exactly the matching streams and upgraded sockets, and that loopback index and `/connect` requests consult a loaded provider and receive its `setCookie`. Covers the reach response headers, the full policy text and a fresh nonce per response, on admitted, pre-login and refused responses and refused upgrades. Lead verdict: keep, after two independent review rounds (2026-11-07); the lead reviews this file line by line before it merges.

Admission seam (C4): `openListener` opens additional listeners on the same routes, bound only to an OS-assigned port on `127.0.0.1` or to handed-in byte streams with TLS at the listener, never to a configured host or port. Each listener's gate decides every request and upgrade request before any route, upgrade handler or the fallback: a refusal dispatches nothing, a pass may carry the Peer resources receive, headers pinned through the route's own, and an `only` route outside which the gate's refusal answers. Dispatch moves into `dispatchRequest` and `dispatchUpgrade`, which the configured listener uses without a gate, so its behaviour is unchanged. Every upgrade socket of an additional listener gets its error handler and is tracked before the gate runs, a refused upgrade is destroyed once its refusal is written, and ids are reserved before the bind, so a reset or half-open refused client cannot crash the process or hold close open, and two opens of one id cannot both bind. A pass decision may carry a nonce, which the index renderer receives for that response through an async-local store. Lead verdict: keep, after two independent review rounds (2026-11-07); the lead reviews this file line by line before it merges.

Admission seam (C4): proves that an additional listener's gate runs before every route, upgrade and the fallback, that refusals and `only` dispatch nothing else, that a pass's Peer and pinned headers reach the response, that `streams` listeners end TLS and expose SNI, that close and service disposal end every connection, and that the configured listener stays ungated. It also proves that refused upgrades reset at once raise no uncaught error, that a half-open refused client is destroyed and close settles, and that a concurrent open of one id fails. Covers the nonce on every inline element the index renderer emits. Lead verdict: keep, after two independent review rounds (2026-11-07); the lead reviews this file line by line before it merges.

Protected home and denied sockets (C1's confinement rules): each dialect's profile builder takes a resolved `Protection`: bwrap binds `/dev/null` over each denied socket's resolved path (never its directory) and mounts an empty tmpfs over the home, binds its readable entries read-only and remounts it read-only; Landlock replaces its `/` read grant, and any write grant containing the home, by grants of every entry beside the way to the home, leaving out entries that resolve to the home, inside it or to its ancestors; Seatbelt appends `deny file-write*` and `deny file-read*` on the home after the write allows, allows its readable entries, and denies `network-outbound` to each socket spelling's `remote unix-socket` path literal. `RUNNER_PROTECTION` reports per runner which rules it expresses (Landlock and Windows cannot express the socket rule; Windows does not confine reads). Review of #66: each wrap protects the home's mount and firmlink aliases like the home (bwrap: a read-only tmpfs over each; Landlock: the whole mount that reaches each alias left out, since Landlock rules attach to inodes and that mount's directories are the inodes on the way; Seatbelt: the same denials), shadows each denied socket's mount aliases, drops a readable entry that leads above the home, grants Landlock paths only by resolved path for the launcher's link refusal, and adds `deny file-link file-clone` on the home under Seatbelt. Each wrap's protection carries that alias coverage. Review of #66: `deniedSocketDirectories` denies every socket in Docker Desktop's control-socket directories (the world-writable WSL `host-services/backend.sock` controls the engine): bwrap hides each directory and its mount aliases under a read-only tmpfs, Seatbelt denies each entry present at the wrap, and an unlistable directory fails the wrap closed. Without a protected home the Landlock grants keep upstream's literal `/tmp`; only a protected profile grants resolved paths.

Scheduled-task consent seam: task creation captures the creation preset — the target Session's preset when one is live, otherwise the deployment default that a created Session is pinned to, which is what the first delivery of that Session will run — when the permission-preset service is composed; an update edit re-captures it from the effective target and settles a recorded refusal, so a re-approved task is reviewed against the preset the approval named; without the service, creation and edits store exactly upstream's task.

Scheduled-task consent seam: before a due delivery wakes its Session the runtime asks the composed consent, on the single-delivery path before the message and on the grouped path member by member; a refusal pauses the task without delivering and records the consent's reason and instant on the task, so no later occurrence retries it and the paused task states why it stopped; the single path reports the typed `schedule/consent-refused` error, a delivery that reaches its target settles the recorded refusal, and the preset shim also reads the deployment default a newly opened Session runs. With no consent composed, delivery is exactly upstream's.

Scheduled-task consent seam: a stored task gains the optional `creationPreset`, the permission preset captured at creation or re-captured by the edit that re-approves it, and the optional `consentRefusal`, the reason and instant a refusal paused it; both are absent when nothing recorded them, so stored tasks keep upstream's shape.

Scheduled-task consent seam: an `ask` approval of `schedule_create` or `schedule_edit` names the effect it would create — the recurrence, restated or read from the stored task, the target Session and its preset — through the composed consent, appended to the policy's reason; a created target names the deployment default its opened Session will run, a stored target Session with no live Agent names no preset rather than the caller's, and a delete names nothing because it arms nothing. Allow and deny stay as the policy resolved them, the model-facing task still carries no Host bookkeeping, and with no consent composed the approval text is upstream's. Session-log append tolerance (security review R6): the concurrent-migration check decodes the competing current generation and compares the decoded Session id and event count, instead of accepting any target whose bytes begin with the migrated generation without ever decoding the appended tail. Lead verdict: the independent audit's R6 finding authorizes the change.

Session-log Zstandard bound (security review R5): the synchronous private decoder's per-frame plaintext ceiling becomes the session-log bound where that is lower than the process-wide Buffer maximum, so a crafted frame with a huge compression ratio is refused by this decoder as the public one refuses it. Lead verdict: the independent audit's R5 finding authorizes the change.

Session-log Zstandard bound (security review R5): the public one-shot decoder passes the session-log plaintext bound to `zstdDecompressSync`, so a frame that would expand past it fails validation instead of being allocated. Lead verdict: the independent audit's R5 finding authorizes the change.

Session-log Zstandard bound (security review R5): declares `MAX_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_BYTES` (64 MiB) and applies it to one-shot frame decompression and to torn-final-frame prefix recovery, so no decode path expands a crafted frame without a limit. Upstream's frame scanning, compression options and decoder factory are unchanged. Lead verdict: the independent audit's R5 finding authorizes the change.

Session-log append tolerance (security review R6): covers a target that begins with the migrated generation byte for byte but whose appended material never completes a frame or a JSONL line, in both encodings, and that is now refused rather than accepted. Lead verdict: the independent audit's R6 finding authorizes the change.

Session-log Zstandard bound (security review R5): covers a 2 KiB frame that expands past the plaintext bound, refused by the one-shot decompressor and by both synchronous decoders. Lead verdict: the independent audit's R5 finding authorizes the change.

S2 review of the /api trust fence: a Host header must be a bare authority — no user information, no whitespace or control character, no trailing dot — with exactly one Host line in the raw header list, and a state-changing request on the /api channel must carry the browser's own origin account (an Origin header, or Fetch-Metadata same-origin/none), while a route may accept a cross-site document navigation whose response the initiator's page cannot read. A state-changing /api request that carries neither Origin nor Sec-Fetch-Site is accepted toward a loopback Host or an HTTPS listener, where a Fetch-Metadata browser always sends a marker, and refused toward any other plain-HTTP destination; a marker that is present and not same-origin or none is refused. Lead verdict: pending; no lead review of this change is recorded yet.
